render.prompt: Locked-off 35 mm wide side view, static camera, no push, no zoom, no pan, one single unbroken twelve-second take from this one camera only. Start exactly from the first frame and continue the same continuous take without any cut; the camera never changes position, height or angle. The glassy mountain lake at golden hour, the small wooden rowing boat in the middle distance with the young man in the lime-green bucket hat (soft, round-shouldered, heavy-set, washed-out grey hoodie, giant black headphones round his neck, baggy black cargo shorts, long white tube socks in black slides) seated in it fishing, his can on the seat beside him, and the explorer in the khaki safari jacket and pith helmet fishing from the end of the wooden pier at the right with his legs over the water. For the first four seconds nothing moves but the two fishing lines and the ripples. Then the water beside the boat swells and the vast dark back of a whale rises out of the lake right next to him, taller than the boat, water sheeting off it, and the swell lifts the boat, tips it onto its side and rolls him and his rod into the lake with a splash. The whale slides back under, the boat rights itself empty and rocking, the young man surfaces beside it in his hat, spluttering, and the explorer on the pier never looks round, his rod perfectly still. Sound: lapping water, a reel ticking, a deep rushing surge as the whale rises, a huge splash, a blow of spray, spluttering, then the lake settling.
